Even setting the location issue aside, the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup point for 0 seconds after the tap, so the required continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point (iii) is not met; his 4 minutes stationary were spent 350 m away.

The driver's written claim that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the system records of his position at the tap and his stationary location, and system records win over the statement.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" and did wait, as the timeline and his own statement record: the tap was at 08:47:20 (F5) and he then stood stationary until he cancelled at 08:51:00 (F2, F3), so the conduct element of a no-show cancellation (NS-1(i)) is on record rather than merely asserted after the fact (F12).

The waiting period itself was longer than three minutes: he was stationary for 4 min 0 s from 08:47:00 to 08:51:00 (F2) and cancelled at 08:51:00, 7 min 0 s after accepting at 08:44:00 (F3), so the duration element of NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the timeline.

The rider knew where to go and simply did not come out: the driver messaged at 08:47 "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please" (F8) and the rider replied at 08:48 only that no car was there (F9), after which no message shows the rider ever walked to the driver's position before the 08:51 cancellation (F3, F11).

The rider's complaint that the driver "was never at the pickup point" is contradicted not only by the rider's own account of waiting there the whole time but by the fact that the driver was stationary for four minutes just 350 m away (F2) in fair weather (F15) on a route with no incidents or congestion (F13, F14), so no external cause kept the driver from the bay.

The cancellation fee on record is $6.61 (F3, F6) with no surge applied (F7), i.e. the ordinary published no-show fee and not an inflated or manual add-on, so the amount itself is not challengeable under FARE-1.

The driver has 1,346 days of account age, a 4.85 rating, 992 trips in 90 days and zero disputes in 90 days (F17), which supports leaving his account untouched; correspondingly the rider has 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F16), so the fee is not a pattern of over-charging by this driver.

weaknesses: NS-1(ii) fails on the system record: at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the driver was 351 m from the pickup point (F5), the threshold is 200 m, and the timeline states driver_arrived_at is null (F4) — the court will read the tap as premature, which is the strongest fact against us.

The GPS record shows he never came within 200 m, his closest approach being 319 m at 08:46:50 (F1), and he stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap (F5), so NS-1(iii)'s "continuously at the pickup point" requirement is not met on the face of the data.

F5 also means the other side can invoke NS-2's additional consequence — a flag_account referral for tapping the arrival button while GPS puts him outside the pickup radius — so we should not be surprised if the rider asks for that, and the rider's chat message F9 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here") plus F4 support the rider's version, not the driver's statement F12.

The driver's own message F8 ("Reached already") sent at 08:47 while he was roughly 350 m away (F2) is an inaccurate arrival claim the court can weigh against his credibility; F12 adds little because a driver's post-hoc statement cannot cure a GPS contradiction.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 7 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded only as to the tap existing, not as to validity: NS-1(i) is not satisfied by a tap alone when F5 shows it was made 351 m from the pickup point and F4 shows the platform never recorded an arrival — the tap must be at the pickup location to count. [F5 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D2: Duration is meaningless without place: NS-1(iii) requires continuous waiting at the pickup point, and F5 records 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap while F2 places the whole 4-minute stationary period 350 m away, so the (iii) element fails. [F2 F5 F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D3: The rider did exactly what NS-1 contemplates — she was at the pickup point and said so at 08:48 (F9) — while the driver's 08:47 "Reached already" message (F8) is contradicted by F2, which puts him 350 m away, and system records beat statements. [F9 F8 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D4: F2 does not help the driver: a stationary position 350 m from the pickup point is not the pickup point, and F1 shows he never came within 200 m at all, closest being 319 m; F13/F14/F15 merely remove an excuse for the failure to reach the bay. [F2 F1 F13 F14 F15] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D5: We do not dispute the arithmetic — $6.61 with no surge (F6, F7) is the published fee — but NS-0 and NS-2 make the fee conditional on NS-1 being satisfied, and on these records it is not, so the amount being ordinary does not make it chargeable. [F6 F7 F3] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2 FARE-1]
→ D6: Profile facts cannot decide the fee question (NS-2 turns on the tap location and wait, not on reputation), and the driver's 992 trips with 0 disputes (F17) neither cures the 351 m tap in F5 nor bars the NS-2 flag_account consequence. [F17 F5 F16] [NS-2]
→ C8: I withdraw C8's reference to profile facts as unnecessary: the NS-2 account flag is supported independently by F5 and F4, and the driver's history is irrelevant to the rider's refund. [F5 F4] [NS-2]
Revised ask: refund_full $6.61

points.response: Conceded only as to the tap existing, not as to validity: NS-1(i) is not satisfied by a tap alone when F5 shows it was made 351 m from the pickup point and F4 shows the platform never recorded an arrival — the tap must be at the pickup location to count.

Duration is meaningless without place: NS-1(iii) requires continuous waiting at the pickup point, and F5 records 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap while F2 places the whole 4-minute stationary period 350 m away, so the (iii) element fails.

The rider did exactly what NS-1 contemplates — she was at the pickup point and said so at 08:48 (F9) — while the driver's 08:47 "Reached already" message (F8) is contradicted by F2, which puts him 350 m away, and system records beat statements.

F2 does not help the driver: a stationary position 350 m from the pickup point is not the pickup point, and F1 shows he never came within 200 m at all, closest being 319 m; F13/F14/F15 merely remove an excuse for the failure to reach the bay.

We do not dispute the arithmetic — $6.61 with no surge (F6, F7) is the published fee — but NS-0 and NS-2 make the fee conditional on NS-1 being satisfied, and on these records it is not, so the amount being ordinary does not make it chargeable.

Profile facts cannot decide the fee question (NS-2 turns on the tap location and wait, not on reputation), and the driver's 992 trips with 0 disputes (F17) neither cures the 351 m tap in F5 nor bars the NS-2 flag_account consequence.
I withdraw C8's reference to profile facts as unnecessary: the NS-2 account flag is supported independently by F5 and F4, and the driver's history is irrelevant to the rider's refund.

events.title: Driver Advocate rebuttal: 9 points
events.body:
→ C1: The rider's version of events is not the only reading of the same records: F1 shows the driver's closest approach at 319 m and F4 shows no platform arrival record, but F5 records a deliberate "I'm Here" tap and F2 records a stationary period, which is consistent with a driver waiting at the Waterway Point access road he could reach rather than the pin; the fee turns on whether the driver discharged his waiting obligation in substance, not on an unpublished radius. [F1 F4 F5 F2] [NS-1]
→ C2: The rider reads the 200 m figure from unchecked data-layer parameters (G2) and treats the tap as fraudulent, but the record shows a driver who messaged the rider first at 08:47 (F8) and waited until 08:51 (F2, F3) — that is not the stationary-and-uncontactable conduct NS-2 targets; this is a genuine waiting dispute, and a malfunction in the app's arrival detection is not the same as tapping a button on a whim. [F5 F8 F2 F3] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ C3: The rider converts a 200 m data parameter (G2) into the legal test, but NS-1(iii) is about whether the driver waited beyond the waiting period before cancelling — he was stationary 4 min 0 s from 08:47:00 to 08:51:00 (F2) and cancelled at 08:51:00, 7 minutes after accepting (F3); if the court will not accept the tap location, the fair result is to send the case to a person rather than to call the driver a fraudster. [F2 F3 F5] [NS-1]
→ C4: The statement (F12) is contradicted only on location at the tap (F5), not on the waiting itself: the driver's chat timeline, with a "I'm Here"-style message at 08:47 (F8) and a cancellation message at 08:50 (F10), was entered contemporaneously and matches the stationary record at 08:47–08:51 (F2), so the system records support the driver on everything except the exact metres. [F12 F5 F8 F10 F2] [NS-1]
→ C5: The rider's own message (F9) says only "I'm at the pickup point, no car here" — it does not say the rider looked for or approached the blue Prius named in F8, and the rider never messaged that they were walking over during the four minutes the driver was stationary (F2, F11); a rider who stays put and refuses to move to the vehicle is exactly the failure to show up that no-show rules address. [F9 F8 F2 F11] [NS-1 NS-0]
→ C6: Refund is not the only outcome: the fee charged ($6.61, F3, F6, with no surge, F7) is the published no-show amount, and where the arrival radius (G2) is the decisive contested parameter but the driver plainly waited and was plainly contactable (F2, F8, F10), NS-1 and NS-2 give the court no automatic full refund; at most the case is undetermined on location and should go to a person (G12). So I ask for no_action, or in the alternative escalate. [F3 F6 F7 F2 F8 F10] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ C7 (concedes): I do not contest that the complaint is timely and that any refund would be a voucher (F3, F6) — that affects the form of relief only, not whether the fee stands. [F3 F6] [NS-7]
→ C8: The rider is right that the profile cannot excuse conduct (F17), and I do not ask it to; I cite the profile (F17) only to resist any flag_account or account action, since the 992 trips in 90 days with zero disputes show no pattern of fee abuse. [F17] [RD-6]
→ C9: The absence of traffic or weather excuses (F13, F14, F15) is irrelevant to our defence, which is not a reroute justification but that the driver did tap (F5) and did wait 4 min 0 s (F2) before cancelling (F3). [F13 F14 F15 F5 F2 F3] [NS-1]

The rider's own message (F9) says only "I'm at the pickup point, no car here" — it does not say the rider looked for or approached the blue Prius named in F8, and the rider never messaged that they were walking over during the four minutes the driver was stationary (F2, F11); a rider who stays put and refuses to move to the vehicle is exactly the failure to show up that no-show rules address.

Refund is not the only outcome: the fee charged ($6.61, F3, F6, with no surge, F7) is the published no-show amount, and where the arrival radius (G2) is the decisive contested parameter but the driver plainly waited and was plainly contactable (F2, F8, F10), NS-1 and NS-2 give the court no automatic full refund; at most the case is undetermined on location and should go to a person (G12). I do not contest that the complaint is timely and that any refund would be a voucher (F3, F6) — that affects the form of relief only, not whether the fee stands.

The rider is right that the profile cannot excuse conduct (F17), and I do not ask it to; I cite the profile (F17) only to resist any flag_account or account action, since the 992 trips in 90 days with zero disputes show no pattern of fee abuse.

The absence of traffic or weather excuses (F13, F14, F15) is irrelevant to our defence, which is not a reroute justification but that the driver did tap (F5) and did wait 4 min 0 s (F2) before cancelling (F3).

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the arrival confirmation; (iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 no-show cancellation fee cannot stand because the driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach was 319 m and he never came within 200 m, and the platform recorded no arrival (driver_arrived_at is null).

The driver's "I'm Here" tap at 08:47:20 was made 351 m from the pickup point, so NS-1 (ii) fails on the tap itself; a tap away from the pickup point is exactly the abuse-of-cancellation-button conduct NS-2 attaches a flag_account to.

Even setting the location issue aside, the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup point for 0 seconds after the tap, so the required continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point (iii) is not met; his 4 minutes stationary were spent 350 m away.

The driver's written claim that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the system records of his position at the tap and his stationary location, and system records win over the statement.

My client was physically at the pickup point and said so in the app at 08:48 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here"), while the driver's “Reached already” message at 08:47 was false as he was 350 m away; the rider did not fail to show up.
Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not all satisfied, the rider is not liable for any cancellation fee and the $6.61 already charged must be refunded in full.
The dispute was filed as a no-show fee complaint (trip 08:51, fee $6.61), within the 30-day window in NS-7, so it is properly before the tribunal; the refund is to be issued as a Ryde voucher.

The driver's history (992 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes upheld) may explain the conduct but does not excuse it; the account flag in NS-2 rests on the recorded tap away from the pickup point, not on the profile facts.
No traffic or weather excuse can assist the driver here, since no incidents or speed-band records exist near the route and the weather was fair (0.0 mm rain).

weaknesses: The driver's consistent story in chat and in his statement (F8, F10, F12) is that he arrived and waited, and the chat record is complete (F11), so the judge must rely squarely on the GPS/timeline contradiction (F1, F2, F5) rather than on the absence of any driver admission.

The 200 m arrival radius and the 3:01 continuous-wait threshold are data-layer parameters (G2), not published Ryde figures, so the driver could argue his 351 m position still counted as "at" the pickup point; the counter is that the same record shows 0 seconds within 200 m.

The driver did wait 4 minutes stationary (F2) and did tap "I'm Here" (F5); if the judge discounts the GPS radius entirely, the remaining dispute turns on whether the stationary location 350 m from the pickup point (F2) can be treated as the pickup point at all.
The rider's own profile shows 1 prior dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld (F16), which the driver could use to suggest a pattern of fee complaints.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" and did wait, as the timeline and his own statement record: the tap was at 08:47:20 (F5) and he then stood stationary until he cancelled at 08:51:00 (F2, F3), so the conduct element of a no-show cancellation (NS-1(i)) is on record rather than merely asserted after the fact (F12).

The waiting period itself was longer than three minutes: he was stationary for 4 min 0 s from 08:47:00 to 08:51:00 (F2) and cancelled at 08:51:00, 7 min 0 s after accepting at 08:44:00 (F3), so the duration element of NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the timeline.

The rider knew where to go and simply did not come out: the driver messaged at 08:47 "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please" (F8) and the rider replied at 08:48 only that no car was there (F9), after which no message shows the rider ever walked to the driver's position before the 08:51 cancellation (F3, F11).

The rider's complaint that the driver "was never at the pickup point" is contradicted not only by the rider's own account of waiting there the whole time but by the fact that the driver was stationary for four minutes just 350 m away (F2) in fair weather (F15) on a route with no incidents or congestion (F13, F14), so no external cause kept the driver from the bay.

The cancellation fee on record is $6.61 (F3, F6) with no surge applied (F7), i.e. the ordinary published no-show fee and not an inflated or manual add-on, so the amount itself is not challengeable under FARE-1.

The driver has 1,346 days of account age, a 4.85 rating, 992 trips in 90 days and zero disputes in 90 days (F17), which supports leaving his account untouched; correspondingly the rider has 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F16), so the fee is not a pattern of over-charging by this driver.

weaknesses: NS-1(ii) fails on the system record: at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the driver was 351 m from the pickup point (F5), the threshold is 200 m, and the timeline states driver_arrived_at is null (F4) — the court will read the tap as premature, which is the strongest fact against us.

The GPS record shows he never came within 200 m, his closest approach being 319 m at 08:46:50 (F1), and he stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap (F5), so NS-1(iii)'s "continuously at the pickup point" requirement is not met on the face of the data.

F5 also means the other side can invoke NS-2's additional consequence — a flag_account referral for tapping the arrival button while GPS puts him outside the pickup radius — so we should not be surprised if the rider asks for that, and the rider's chat message F9 ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here") plus F4 support the rider's version, not the driver's statement F12.

The driver's own message F8 ("Reached already") sent at 08:47 while he was roughly 350 m away (F2) is an inaccurate arrival claim the court can weigh against his credibility; F12 adds little because a driver's post-hoc statement cannot cure a GPS contradiction.

points.response: Conceded only as to the tap existing, not as to validity: NS-1(i) is not satisfied by a tap alone when F5 shows it was made 351 m from the pickup point and F4 shows the platform never recorded an arrival — the tap must be at the pickup location to count.

Duration is meaningless without place: NS-1(iii) requires continuous waiting at the pickup point, and F5 records 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap while F2 places the whole 4-minute stationary period 350 m away, so the (iii) element fails.

The rider did exactly what NS-1 contemplates — she was at the pickup point and said so at 08:48 (F9) — while the driver's 08:47 "Reached already" message (F8) is contradicted by F2, which puts him 350 m away, and system records beat statements.

F2 does not help the driver: a stationary position 350 m from the pickup point is not the pickup point, and F1 shows he never came within 200 m at all, closest being 319 m; F13/F14/F15 merely remove an excuse for the failure to reach the bay.

We do not dispute the arithmetic — $6.61 with no surge (F6, F7) is the published fee — but NS-0 and NS-2 make the fee conditional on NS-1 being satisfied, and on these records it is not, so the amount being ordinary does not make it chargeable.

Profile facts cannot decide the fee question (NS-2 turns on the tap location and wait, not on reputation), and the driver's 992 trips with 0 disputes (F17) neither cures the 351 m tap in F5 nor bars the NS-2 flag_account consequence.
I withdraw C8's reference to profile facts as unnecessary: the NS-2 account flag is supported independently by F5 and F4, and the driver's history is irrelevant to the rider's refund.

The rider's version of events is not the only reading of the same records: F1 shows the driver's closest approach at 319 m and F4 shows no platform arrival record, but F5 records a deliberate "I'm Here" tap and F2 records a stationary period, which is consistent with a driver waiting at the Waterway Point access road he could reach rather than the pin; the fee turns on whether the driver discharged his waiting obligation in substance, not on an unpublished radius.

The rider reads the 200 m figure from unchecked data-layer parameters (G2) and treats the tap as fraudulent, but the record shows a driver who messaged the rider first at 08:47 (F8) and waited until 08:51 (F2, F3) — that is not the stationary-and-uncontactable conduct NS-2 targets; this is a genuine waiting dispute, and a malfunction in the app's arrival detection is not the same as tapping a button on a whim.

The rider converts a 200 m data parameter (G2) into the legal test, but NS-1(iii) is about whether the driver waited beyond the waiting period before cancelling — he was stationary 4 min 0 s from 08:47:00 to 08:51:00 (F2) and cancelled at 08:51:00, 7 minutes after accepting (F3); if the court will not accept the tap location, the fair result is to send the case to a person rather than to call the driver a fraudster.

The statement (F12) is contradicted only on location at the tap (F5), not on the waiting itself: the driver's chat timeline, with a "I'm Here"-style message at 08:47 (F8) and a cancellation message at 08:50 (F10), was entered contemporaneously and matches the stationary record at 08:47–08:51 (F2), so the system records support the driver on everything except the exact metres.

The rider's own message (F9) says only "I'm at the pickup point, no car here" — it does not say the rider looked for or approached the blue Prius named in F8, and the rider never messaged that they were walking over during the four minutes the driver was stationary (F2, F11); a rider who stays put and refuses to move to the vehicle is exactly the failure to show up that no-show rules address.

Refund is not the only outcome: the fee charged ($6.61, F3, F6, with no surge, F7) is the published no-show amount, and where the arrival radius (G2) is the decisive contested parameter but the driver plainly waited and was plainly contactable (F2, F8, F10), NS-1 and NS-2 give the court no automatic full refund; at most the case is undetermined on location and should go to a person (G12). So I ask for no_action, or in the alternative escalate.
I do not contest that the complaint is timely and that any refund would be a voucher (F3, F6) — that affects the form of relief only, not whether the fee stands.

The rider is right that the profile cannot excuse conduct (F17), and I do not ask it to; I cite the profile (F17) only to resist any flag_account or account action, since the 992 trips in 90 days with zero disputes show no pattern of fee abuse.

The absence of traffic or weather excuses (F13, F14, F15) is irrelevant to our defence, which is not a reroute justification but that the driver did tap (F5) and did wait 4 min 0 s (F2) before cancelling (F3).

Records also show he never waited inside the pickup area after tapping. So the fee was not chargeable. You were at the pickup point and did the right thing by saying so. A $6.61 Ryde voucher is being issued to you. Nothing further is needed from you.
